newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA says monetary policy broadly appropriate.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA says monetary policy broadly appropriate.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) said on Tuesday that Australia's monetary policy was broadly appropriate.

In its February Bulletin, which contained its quarterly report on the economy, the RBA said it also expected a good performance on inflation in the near term. It said it expected underlying inflation to be in the two to three percent band in 1998. On employment, the bank said underlying employment growth seems to have picked up. However, it said the union "living wage claim" would adversely affect employment.
The RBA said retail sales weakness was unlikely to continue.
The bank also said it saw evidence that the housing sector was in the early stage of an upturn.

"Given this assessment of the outlook for inflation and growth, and the uncertainties still surrounding wage outcomes, the bank sees current monetary policy settings as broadly appropriate for the time being," the bank said.
"Information becoming available recently points to a somewhat stronger tone in economic activity than appeared to be the case for much of 1996," the bank said.
"In the near term, the bank expects the recent good performance on inflation to be maintained.
"On current indications, barring unforeseen changes in the exchange rate or labour costs, underlying inflation could be maintained around two percent during 1997.
"At this point, the bank expects inflation to be in the two to three percent range in 1998," the central bank.

The bank said the labour market had been lacklustre for some time. "But the most recent two quarters were a good deal stronger than their predecessors, even without adjusting for apparent under-reporting.
"Although monthly numbers are extremely volatile, underlying employment growth seems to have picked up," the bank said.
unemployment rate was 8.6 perdcent in January.

The RBA said wage costs needed to be contained for economic recovery to be sustained. "On average, results over 1996 have been satisfactory, although outcomes from enterprise bargaining in the private sector seem to be higher than aggregate inflation and productivity trends would sustainably permit," it said.

"A rise in other types of wages, which pushed them near to the increases achieved in enterprise agreements, would lead to an aggregate wage outcome which was inconsistent with the inflation objective, and so have implications for future monetary policy," the RBA said.
The bank said retail spending slowed through 1996, culminating in a fall in the December quarter.
"This degree of weakness is unlikely to continue, and most retailers have reported a better start to the new year.
"Private investment particularly non-residential construction has been very strong, and all indications are that it will remain so," the central bank.

"At the same time, housing construction, which has been weak for around two years, is now starting to show the first sigbs of recovery in the form of increased loan and building approvals," the Reserve Bank said.
